Question B-006-009-003.

Why the correct answer is right: A parasitic element that is slightly shorter than the driven half-wave element acts as a director. In a Yagi, radiation is strengthened from the driven dipole toward the director.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "From the new element towards the dipole": That reverses the director action. Radiation toward the dipole from the new element would describe the effect of a reflector placed on the opposite side.
- sourceIndex 2: "In both directions at right angles to the elements": A plain dipole has broadside maxima at right angles to the wire, but adding a shorter parasitic element changes the system into an end-fire beam toward that element.
- sourceIndex 3: "In both directions parallel to the elements": The ends of a half-wave element are near the dipole nulls. A director increases radiation along the boom direction, not out from the wire ends.
